chapter_theme: A song for the seven shrines (சப்தஸ்தானம்) around Thiruvaiyaru: the poet asks not to approach scheming courtesans and to be given the joy of singing again the Thiruppugazh he sang at Arunai; the praise names the seven shrines one by one.

886.reading: The poet describes courtesans with deceit in their hearts, spear eyes and sweet words, who call everyone on the street, spread their desire for money and read every trick of maya, and asks not to approach them but, thinking on the lotus feet, to sing in calm joy the Thiruppugazh he sang before at Arunai. The praise names Murugan the bridegroom of Valli, with whom he stayed on her platform and wandered every forest, at whose thought the asuras' houses fell to dust and the gods' land rained gold, and the lord of the seven shrines of Thiruvaiyaru: Pazhanam, Chotruthurai, Vedikudi, Kandiyur where Brahma's head fell, Poonthuruthi, Neyththanam and Thiruvaiyaru itself.
886.nuance: முன் அருணை நாடதில் ஓது திருப்புகழ்: the poet refers to his own earlier songs at Tiruvannamalai, where the book's tradition places the start of the Thiruppugazh. The seven shrines are named by allusion: அயிலு சோறு for Chotruthurai, மறை தேடிய ... குடி for Vedikudi, விதி ஆதிச் சிரமும் மாநிலம் வீழ்தரு for Kandiyur, நெய்ப்பதி for Neyththanam. The asura line (உழவர் சாகரமோடி ஒளித்திட) is obscure.
